title: When should the orchestrator hand off besides the 60% threshold?
context: After a long idle stretch the prompt cache has expired, so the next message makes a long-running orchestrator re-read its whole context (hundreds of thousands of tokens), which is slow and costly. A fresh orchestrator starts from the board index and a handoff instead. Amends decision 10, which hands off only at the 60% context threshold.

options.name: When Matt says so
options.summary: Matt says hand off, at the end of the day or any time.

options.name: Automatically after a long idle stretch
options.summary: If the orchestrator has been idle for 3 hours and is above 25% context, it writes the handoff and retires; the next message goes to a fresh orchestrator. Matt can still say hand off any time. The 60% threshold stays.
pros: Avoids the costly cold re-read after nights and long breaks
cons: May hand off during a long break

recommendation: Handles the overnight case without Matt thinking about it; the floor keeps it from churning on light days.
reason: B, with the idle window at 3 hours and the floor at 25%

settles.value: hand off automatically after 3 hours idle when above 25% context, in addition to the 60% threshold and on the human's word
